principles: One normative source per process fact
Host discovery compatibility without host-specific truth duplication
Operational guidance must be mechanically verifiable
drivers: B-e514 is blocked by an obsolete root-document process-fact contract
Codex, Claude Code, and Antigravity/agy use asymmetric native discovery filenames
Maintainers need a concrete migration order rather than another conceptual document
Root entrypoints must retain non-negotiable safety constraints without regrowing into manuals

options.name: A: Single all-in-one migration Story
cons: Large overlapping diff across docs, templates, runtime, prompts, and tests
Hard to review and roll back

options.name: B: Registry-first staged migration
pros: Establishes one canonical-doc registry before moving consumers
Allows red tests and compatibility reads before root cutover
Provides clean rollback points and a controlled B-e514 convergence path

rationale: A registry-first staged migration separates normative sources, operational projections, host adapters, mechanical consumers, and final root cutover. It prevents root documents from being thinned before audit/verifier consumers can follow canonical sources, while keeping every implementation slice reviewable and reversible.

preMortem.scenario: The runbook becomes a third independent lifecycle specification.
preMortem.trigger: The runbook copies phase, reviewer, or DONE semantics without deriving or validating them against canonical registries and decisions.
preMortem.consequence: Root documents become thin but process drift simply moves into docs/dev.
preMortem.mitigation: Classify the runbook as a non-normative operational projection and require command, phase, lane, link, and policy checks against a shared canonical-doc/process registry.

preMortem.scenario: B-e514 overwrites or conflicts with the migrated root entrypoints.
preMortem.trigger: The contract migration and B-e514 both modify AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md or close in the wrong order.
preMortem.consequence: One Story invalidates the other evidence or restores stale entrypoint content.
preMortem.mitigation: The plan must choose a single root-cutover owner, explicitly supersede or sequence B-e514, and prohibit overlapping root-file writes until that ownership is resolved.

preMortem.scenario: Claude loses mandatory project safety instructions after CLAUDE.md is shortened.
preMortem.trigger: CLAUDE.md becomes a pointer but its AGENTS import or canonical-link closure is missing or untested.
preMortem.consequence: Claude sessions omit session recovery, controlled story writes, or other repository constraints.
preMortem.mitigation: Test effective host instruction closure, including Claude imports, rather than checking only literal text in each file.

preMortem.scenario: A canonical registry is added but legacy consumers continue scanning only CLAUDE.md.
preMortem.trigger: Audit, docs-drift, reviewer prompts, sync utilities, or verifier path arrays are missed during inventory.
preMortem.consequence: The migration appears complete while some gates and diagnostics retain the old contract.
preMortem.mitigation: Include repository-wide hard-code inventory, consumer-by-consumer migration acceptance, and a final negative scan for semantic CLAUDE.md truth-source dependencies.
